paragraphs: Begin with a morning briefing on the day's schedule. In the morning, review orders and contraindications, help patients onto the table, move them into the magnet, set sequences, and monitor images. Continue examinations after midday, slowing down to reassure patients with claustrophobia. Adjust parameters and repeat blurred slices in the afternoon. Before leaving, complete quality control, archive images, and schedule the next day's specialized scans.

In short, they use magnetic fields to create clear images of the human body.
